newsitem.title: USA: Furon to acquire Medex for $160 million.
newsitem.headline: Furon to acquire Medex for $160 million.

text.p: Furon Co. said Wednesday it agreed to acquire Medex Inc., another maker of health care products and components, in a cash tender offer valued at $160 million.

Under the definitive agreement, Furon's FCY Inc. unit will offer $23.50 a share for all of Medex's outstanding common stock. This puts the offer at a premium of about 59 percent to Medex's average trading price over the last 30 days.
Medex soared $7.84 to $23.09 on Nasdaq in late morning trading. Furon fell 25 cents to $20.75 on the New York Stock Exchange.
After the offer expires, Furon will acquire any remaining Medex shares at the same price as paid in the tender offer.
The deal has been approved by the boards of directors of each company, and remains subject to approval by holders of at least 60 percent of Medex's shares as well as regulators.
Medex is required to pay an $8.0 million breakup fee under some circumstances.

Medex, based in Hilliard, Ohio, makes polymer-based critical care products and infusion systems for medical and surgical use that are sold in over 50 countries. It had sales of $99.3 million in its fiscal year ended June.

"Medex has excellent channels to market directly to health care providers," Michael Hagan, Furon's chief executive, said in a statement. "From this base, we can accelerate growth with new products, product line extensions and market penetration."

Laguna Niguel, Calif.-based Furon makes polymer components for products in several industries including health care. These include shunts, catheters, tubing and other medical products primarily for original equipment manufacturers. It had sales of $345 million for its fiscal year ended Feb. 3.
